---
title: "Classifying codes with an LLM ensemble"
format: html
---

Assigns every USRDS primary-cause code to its USRDS primary disease group, using USRDS's own assignments where they exist and three large language models for the rest, for review by the deciders ([#D4]). The paper's six categories follow from the groups. It is run once, by hand, because it calls paid APIs; the reviewed file in `references/` is what the analysis reads.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/classify_esrd_causes.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/classify_esrd_causes.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/functions.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/classify_esrd_causes.R")
```

## ellmer version

The script needs ellmer 0.4.2 or later. From that version, ellmer uses Anthropic's own structured output for current Claude models; earlier versions force a tool call, which these models reject.

```{r}
#| label: check-ellmer-version
#| eval: false
```

## The approach

The paper's six cause categories are not a standard grouping, but they collapse a standard one. CMS's list of primary causes of renal failure for the CMS-2728 form sorts the causes into named groups, which USRDS uses as its primary disease groups: diabetes, glomerulonephritis, secondary glomerulonephritis and vasculitis, interstitial nephritis and pyelonephritis, hypertension and large vessel disease, cystic, hereditary and congenital diseases, neoplasms, transplant complications, and miscellaneous conditions [@cms2728_causes]. The classification therefore happens in two steps:

1.  **Each code gets its USRDS group.** USRDS has assigned a group to the codes on the current form, mostly ICD-10-CM; those are used as they are. The three models assign the others, mostly ICD-9-CM codes from older forms, with USRDS's own assignments as their reference.
2.  **Each group gets a paper category**, decided once by the deciders in [`references/usrds-cause-groups.csv`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/references/usrds-cause-groups.csv) ([#D4]). The analysis reads the category through the group, so a change to that table needs no new model run.

## The code list

The original mapping spreadsheet is lost. Its replacement starts from public lists in Appendix C of the Researcher's Guide, which `usRds` already holds: every code of format `$PD96DET` with its description, and USRDS's group for each code of format `PD_SUBGROUP` [@usrds2024guide]. Each code is labelled with its coding system. No patient data are involved, and the list is not filtered by what appears in the data.

```{r}
#| label: load-cause-codes
```

## The prompt

All three models receive the same prompt, word for word. It is kept as a text file, [`prompts/esrd-cause-classification.md`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/prompts/esrd-cause-classification.md), so that it can be read and edited on its own and shown here exactly as sent:

```{verbatim}
#| file: ../prompts/esrd-cause-classification.md
#| lang: markdown
```

Three parts are filled in for each batch:

-   `{{group_list}}`: the USRDS groups, each with examples of what it contains.
-   `{{reference_list}}`: every code USRDS has grouped, as a worked example, for instance `M3131 [ICD-10-CM]: WEGENER'S GRANULOMATOSIS WITH RENAL INVOLVEMENT -> Secondary GN/vasculitis`.
-   `{{code_list}}`: the batch of codes to classify, each with its coding system and USRDS description, for instance `4464Z [ICD-9-CM, USRDS variant]: WEGENERS GRANULOMATOSIS`.

The prompt's rules:

-   **Group like USRDS.** Each code goes to the group USRDS uses for the same condition in the reference list, so ICD-9-CM and ICD-10-CM codes for one condition, and all USRDS variants of a code, land in the same group.
-   **Use knowledge of the named condition, not guesses about the cause.** A first version of the prompt told the models to classify "from the code and its description only". They became literal: vasculitis, lupus without a named nephritis, and congenital anomalies went to "Other" whenever the description did not name a category. The models may now use what is known about the named condition (which disease a syndrome is), but not invent a cause the description does not name.
-   **Say when a description is ambiguous.** Some USRDS descriptions name two conditions (for example, "BUERGER'S (BERGER'S) DISEASE"); the model chooses one and says so in its reason, for the deciders to check.
-   **Separate unknown causes from invalid ones**: codes for missing or unknown causes, and codes that are not a cause of kidney failure, such as chronic kidney disease stages.

## Prompt and schema in code

The structured output schema restricts each answer to the USRDS group names, and the check below confirms it. Each saved answer file carries a short fingerprint of the prompt text, so an edited prompt is sent to every provider again.

```{r}
#| label: define-classification-prompt
#| eval: false
```

## One function per provider

The same three providers as the USRDS-PDF-analysis-project ensemble, each with its current general-purpose model, set in `setup.R` [@ellmer_pkg]. Each has its own function, so each provider can be run, checked and saved on its own.

```{r}
#| label: define-providers
#| eval: false
```

## Running and saving each provider

Each provider runs and is checked on its own: every code answered exactly once, no invented codes, only the six categories. Its answers are then saved under the provider and model name, so a rerun after a failure asks only the providers that have not finished.

```{r}
#| label: classify-with-ensemble
#| eval: false
```

## Agreement

A code keeps USRDS's own group where it has one. Otherwise its group is accepted when all three models agree, and the rest are left for the deciders, who fill `final_group` and their initials. Agreement among the models is summarized with Fleiss' kappa.

```{r}
#| label: measure-agreement
#| eval: false
```
